evidence: Nestled along the tranquil Bac Hung Hai canal on the outskirts of Hanoi, the Bat Trang Pottery Museum, also known as the Vietnam Craft Village Quintessence Center, stands as a testament to the rich cultural heritage of Vietnam. This magnificent structure, which has only recently emerged in the past few years, continues the legacy of the thousand-year-old ceramic traditions that were established by the ancestors who sailed downstream from Bo Bat to settle in this fertile alluvial plain.

The architectural design of the Bat Trang Pottery Museum is both awe-inspiring and functional, featuring seven colossal spiral blocks that resemble giant potter’s wheels, symbolizing the very essence of the craft. These spiraling blocks are constructed from rustic reddish-brown fired bricks, complemented by light-catching glass panels that reflect the sun’s rays, creating a dynamic interplay of light and shadow throughout the day.
